question: Which of the following countries hosted the first edition of ICC Women's Under-19 Cricket World Cup in 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is __**South Africa.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The first edition of the **ICC Women's Under-19** **Cricket World Cup**, hosted by** South Africa in 2023, **was the 2023 ICC Under-19 Women's T20 World Cup.
 
• Because of the** COVID-19 pandemic**, the tournament was **rescheduled **from the **end **of **2021 **to** January 2023.**
 
• The tournament featured **sixteen teams **that were initially divided into four groups.
 
• **India, England, Australia, **and **New Zealand **advanced to the competition's semi-finals.
 
• **India defeated New Zealand **by 8 wickets in the semi-finals, while England defeated Australia by 3 runs.
 
• The final took place on 29th January 2023 at** Senwes Park, Potchefstroom. **
 
• India beat England in the first-ever ICC U-19 Women’s T20 World Cup .
 
• India bowled out England for a paltry 68 and won by 7 wkts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The tournament was originally scheduled to take place in **January 2021, **but it was pushed back to** December 2021** due to the **COVID-19 pandemic.**
 
• The ICC considered deferring the tournament from its scheduled January 2021 date to later in the year in** November 2020.**
 
• The **Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB)** confirmed in January 2021 that they would host the tournament in December 2021, but the tournament was postponed for the second time, and was moved to January 2023. 
 
• The** ICC's CEO, Geoff Allardice, **stated in January 2022 that the tournament was "very much on the cards," and that the ICC was beginning the search for hosts.
